title: Reducing Target Group Bias in Hate Speech Detectors
measurement_description: Hate speech detection accuracy for different target groups, including religious groups such as Jewish and Muslim individuals.
base_benchmarks: Learning from the Worst (Vidgen et al., 2020)
findings: The baseline BERT-based hate speech detector showed significant performance disparities across different target groups, including religious ones. On the 'LearningWorst' dataset, the baseline model performed well on 'Jew' (83%) and 'Muslim' (79%) groups. On the 'HateXplain' dataset, performance was notably lower for the 'Jewish' group (57%). The paper's proposed token-level debiasing method improved performance and reduced variance, increasing accuracy for the 'Jewish' group to 79% and the 'Muslim' group to 82% on the respective datasets.
